item.title: The Visibility Gap: The Case for a North American Trusted Trade Laboratory
item.description: Supply chain visibility is the best defense against Chinese overcapacity and transshipment. The USMCA Review can act as a coordinating mechanism for North American trade to leverage AI and large-scale data analytics to make supply chains transparent for the first time.

item.title: The Role of Regional Networks in Twenty-First-Century Industrial Policy
item.description: America's next era of technological leadership will be won in its regions. Connecting research, manufacturing, and commercialization through regional innovation ecosystems can help turn scientific breakthroughs into economic and strategic advantage.

item.title: Tokenpolitik: How the United States Can Compete with China to Build the Global AI Stack
item.description: Tokens are the currency of a new international order. As China races to build the global AI stack, the United States needs "tokenpolitik," a grand strategy bridging agencies and private firms to export the U.S. AI stack worldwide and outcompete China’s Digital Silk Road.

item.title: Beyond the Rome Talks: Pilot Zones, Hezbollah, and Rebuilding State Authority in South Lebanon
item.description: The second round of Lebanon-Israel talks in Rome must build on progress towards Israeli withdrawals and Hezbollah disarmament—and represent a test of whether Lebanon can reclaim sovereignty in its own territory.

item.title: The United States’ Accelerating Memory Chip Crunch: Implications for Tech and AI Leadership
item.description: The rapid expansion of AI data centers is creating adverse effects across the memory chip ecosystem. As memory suppliers shift toward high-bandwidth memory, shortages of conventional RAM are raising costs for consumer electronics and fueling calls for government action.

item.title: A Global Forced Labor Import Regime Is Emerging—Can It Work?
item.description: USTR announced sweeping tariffs across 60 economies to address unfair trade practices related to the importation of forced labor-made goods. This presents significant opportunities for promoting workers' rights as well as potentially dire risks to those same rights.
